newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway c.bank governor rejects OECD advise.
newsitem.headline: Norway c.bank governor rejects OECD advise.

text.p: Norwegian central bank governor Kjell Storvik reiterated on Wednesday that fiscal policy, not monetary policy, would be used to stabilise economic developments.

Storvik, in an interview with Norwegian radio, was reacting to an OECD survey which said the booming Norwegian economy was operating near capacity and could start overheating unless a restrictive monetary policy were pursued.
Asked if this was a recipe to follow, Storvik said: "No, it is not simply because it is the fiscal policy that in the first instance shall contribute to stabilising economic developments."

"Monetary policy, and interest rates, is aimed at stabilising the exchange rate of the Norwegian crown against European currencies. It is with this goal in mind that we have reduced rates to contribute to such a stabilisation of the currency exchange rate," he said.

Asked if the central bank would keep key interest rates low for now, Storvik said: "Central banks do not comment on interest rate developments but up till now we have cut interest rates to fulfil the goal we have been given by political authorities, namely to stabilise the exchange rate against European currencies."

The survey by the Organisation of Economic Cooperation and Development said on Monday that Norway's strategy -- with monetary policy focusing on exchange rate stability and fiscal policy geared to inflation control -- was coming under strain now that the risk of inflationary tensions was rising.
"Consequently, a restrictive monetary policy is now necessary," it said.

OECD noted that the central bank's deposit rate, which constitutes the floor for money market rates, had been cut by some 150 basis points since March 1996 in fruitless attempts to keep the petroleum currency from appreciating.

"These developments have contributed to higher asset prices, both in the real estate and stock markets....Therefore, whatever room exists for tightening monetary conditions, within the present framework of maintaining a stable exchange rate over the medium term, needs to be used to forestall an acceleration of inflation," OECD said.
